stories.title: Academy District 20 Back-to-School August 17-18 — Staggered Start

x_posts.label: Post 1-1
x_posts.text:
D20 starts this weekend.

Preschool, elementary, 6th, and 9th graders start Monday, August 17. Everyone else starts Tuesday.

The staggered start gives new students an orientation day before the full school arrives.

#COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text:
Academy District 20 has a two-day back-to-school start.

August 17: preschool, elementary, 6th, and 9th grade.
August 18: all other students.

Back-to-school bags ready. First-day photos loaded.

#COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
📅 D20 families — your first day of school is almost here.

Academy District 20 kicks off the 2026-27 school year with a staggered start. If your child is in preschool, elementary school, 6th grade, or 9th grade, they head in this Monday, August 17. That's the transition-year orientation day — giving students who are new to a school building (or a new grade configuration) a chance to find their footing before the whole school arrives.

Everyone else — 7th grade, 8th grade, 10th, 11th, 12th — starts Tuesday, August 18.

The two-day ramp-up is intentional. It means the first-day energy is spread across fewer students, which makes mornings a little smoother for families navigating a new school, a new classroom, or just a new school year.

If you're doing the back-to-school countdown, you've got the weekend. Who's starting this Monday? Drop a 🎒 in the comments.

article.headline: Academy District 20 Back-to-School 2026: Start Dates, Staggered Schedule, and What to Expect

stories.title: Taleco Gear Baby Jumpers and Swings Recalled — ~41,100 Units, Fall and Strangulation Hazards

x_posts.label: Post 2-1
x_posts.text:
CPSC recall: Stop using Taleco Gear baby jumpers and swings now.

~41,100 units. Falls, impact, and strangulation hazards. 52 incidents, 32 injuries reported.

Contact Taleco Gear for a full refund. Destroy the product.

#COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

x_posts.label: Post 2-2
x_posts.text:
If you bought a Taleco Gear baby jumper or swing on Amazon, Walmart, or TalecoGear.com — stop using it now.

Recalled August 13. Falls, impact, strangulation hazards. Full refund available.

#COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
🚨 If you have a Taleco Gear baby jumper or swing at home, please stop using it right now.

The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission announced a recall on August 13 covering approximately 41,100 Taleco Gear baby jumpers and swings sold in the United States (and 150 more in Canada). The products were sold on Amazon.com, Walmart.com, and TalecoGear.com between April 2021 and July 2026 for $65 to $120. The recall covers three separate hazards: units that become unstable (fall and impact risk), hanging restraint straps that create a strangulation hazard, and seat openings sized to create an entrapment risk for infants. There have been 52 reported incidents and 32 injuries.

Here's how to find out if your product is affected: check the fabric wash/care label inside the seat cover. The model number will be printed there.

If your product is recalled, stop using it immediately and contact Taleco Gear to arrange a full refund. The CPSC's instruction is to destroy the product — not donate it, not resell it, not pass it along to another family.

Please share this post. These products were sold across multiple major retailers over five years, and not every parent who bought one will see this recall automatically.

Did you know this one was recalled? Have you ever had to act on a product recall? 👇
facebook.image_caption: 🚨 RECALL ALERT: Taleco Gear baby jumpers and swings — ~41,100 units recalled August 13. Hazards include falls, strangulation, and entrapment. Sold on Amazon, Walmart, and TalecoGear.com from April 2021 to July 2026. Stop use immediately. Full refund available. Model number is on the fabric label inside the seat cover. Full story at the link.

article.headline: Taleco Gear Baby Jumpers and Swings Recalled: Fall, Impact, and Strangulation Hazards

stories.title: TESSA Pasta in the Park — Tonight, August 15, Myron Stratton Home

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text:
Tonight: Pasta in the Park, 6 PM, Myron Stratton Home, Colorado Springs.

Pasta tasting, live entertainment, auctions. Benefits domestic violence survivors in the Pikes Peak region.

$120 tickets. Hosted by TESSA.

#COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
🍝 If you're looking for something to do tonight in Colorado Springs, TESSA's annual Pasta in the Park is happening at 6 PM at the Myron Stratton Home.

This year's theme is "Shelter from the Storm," and the event benefits domestic violence and sexual assault survivors in the Pikes Peak region. The evening includes a pasta tasting competition, beverages, live entertainment, and both silent and live auctions. TESSA is aiming to raise $150,000 through tonight's fundraiser.

Tickets are $120. If you're in a position to attend — or know someone who is — this is one of the bigger community fundraisers of the summer in Colorado Springs.

TESSA serves survivors across El Paso and Teller counties, providing emergency shelter, advocacy, counseling, and legal support. Their work matters year-round, and tonight's event is a chance to support that directly.

Have you been to Pasta in the Park before? Thinking of going tonight? 🍷

stories.title: D49 Early Childhood Education Opens Two New Preschool Classrooms at Student Success Center

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text:
D49 is adding two new preschool classrooms at the Student Success Center this August.

Classes run Mon–Thu at the permanent SSC campus in east Colorado Springs.

Part of the Falcon Zone long-range plan.

#COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
🏫 Good news for families in east Colorado Springs: D49 Early Childhood Education is adding two new preschool classrooms this August.

The new classrooms are at the Student Success Center, which has now settled into its permanent home in the former Falcon Elementary School of Technology building. (The FESoT campus itself has relocated to Bennett Ranch Elementary.) The new preschool classes run Monday through Thursday, and both are full-time programs.

This expansion is part of the Falcon Zone's long-range facilities plan. That plan includes a projected new PreK-8 school for the area — so these two new classrooms are part of a bigger picture of growing early childhood capacity in the eastern part of the district.

If you have a preschool-aged child in the Falcon area, D49's Early Childhood Education team is worth contacting directly through d49.org for enrollment information.

Does your family use D49 Early Childhood programs? What has your experience been? 💬

stories.title: AAP Updates Screen Time Guidelines — What Colorado Springs Parents Need to Know

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text:
New AAP screen time guidance:

No screens before 18 months. One hour of high-quality content daily for ages 2-5.

Device-free meals and bedrooms. Co-watch. Talk about what you're seeing.

Balance over burnout.

#COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
📱 The American Academy of Pediatrics has updated its screen time guidance — and it's a lot more nuanced than "no more than X minutes per day."

The core recommendations: no screens before 18 months, with the exception of video calls with family. For kids ages 2-5, up to one hour of high-quality programming per day is the guideline. For older children and teens, the focus shifts from strict time limits to balance — making sure screens don't crowd out sleep, physical activity, family time, or unstructured play.

The AAP also emphasizes two practical habits: device-free bedrooms and mealtimes (both for kids and parents), and co-viewing — watching together, talking about what you're seeing, asking questions. Research increasingly shows that how families engage with screens matters as much as how much time is spent on them.

There's a newer framing the AAP uses that's worth keeping in mind: "balance over burnout." The goal isn't zero screens — it's making sure that when screens are part of the day, they're not the only part.

We're all figuring this out in real time. What's your screen time approach at home right now? No judgment — genuinely curious. 💬

For older kids: balance over burnout. Device-free bedrooms and mealtimes. Co-watch and talk about what you're seeing. Full breakdown at the link.

article.headline: AAP Screen Time Guidelines 2026: What Colorado Springs Parents Need to Know
